title: STL Export defaults to Apply Modifiers->Render, should be Apply Modidifers->Viewport
body:
Windows 11

5.2.0 LTS

1.4.0

### Describe the bug

It seems that Blender has added a feature to STL export, and once again the chosen default state of that new features is different than the default state that it was before making the new behavior unexpected.

In Blender 5.2.0 LTE the Apply Modifiers option has been broken out into it's own drop down because they've added a new options. You can apply modifiers based on Render or Viewport. In the past it simply applied modifiers based on the viewport, but now it applies them based on the render. This might be a useful feature in the future, but it's different from the old behavior. It also means that if your object is hidden in the render it doesn't export!

Can the STL export feature in the 3D toolbox either acknowledge this change with it's own associated checkbox and/or dropdown or just use the old behavior?

title: False positive "Zero Faces" in Degenerate check
body: Ubuntu 26.04 5.2.0 1.3.5 ### Describe the bug The Degenerate check uses the same threshold value for two different things: edge length and face area. By default this value is 0.0001 (0.1mm), meant as a "basically zero" length. But area is length squared. Used directly on area, 0.0001 means 100mm², not 0.01mm². So any face smaller than 100mm² gets flagged as "Zero Faces", even normal, healthy geometry. Fix: square the threshold before comparing to face area (in analyze.py): faces_zero = [... if ele.calc_area() <= threshold ** 2] Tested on a mesh with real 95mm² faces (8-26mm edges, nothing degenerate about them) — false positive gone, all other checks unaffected. Unfortunately I cannot create a PR to fix this bug. Maybe, because this a new account to report this bug :) If wanted I can append a patch file if wanted.

title: Geometry Node version of edit tools?
body:
MacOS

5

N/A

### Describe the bug

I looked to see if there was a request for this, even if it was declined. I couldn't find it so I thought of leaving this here even if it gets declined to stay as a marker in case others have the same request.

Essentially what the title says. While Geometry Nodes are used for many things, one of their uses is to build solids for printing in a way that approaches parametric design. For these cases, being able to apply via geometry nodes what would be manual steps is very useful.

Not all of the toolbox applies, but for sure it would be useful to have GNs for Bisect, Hollow and Make manifold, as well as informative versions of the analysis tools that provide data for other GNs to make decisions.

This may be too out there for the scope of the project, but since it's so common to have to "apply" GNs to be able to execute the various fixing routines, maybe it's worth considering (assuming it's something Blender has made simple enough to extend into).

title: Consider adding triangulation
body:
I rely heavily on this addon for my work. I have probably pressed the "Make manifold" many thousand times.

Sometimes this addon removes large flat irregular faces. Say you have a big plane and dig out many holes in it (like bullet holes). Seldom, big faces will be removed. If I go into edit mode first and triangulate it, this will never happen. 

Sometimes, when exporting to STL, new errors will crop up in the exported file, because STL-files are triangulated. So if a quad face is triangulated in a bad way, this error will not be shown when analyzing the model, just in the exported file. The solution is to triangulate it manually.

It would be good if triangulation was controlled by a checkbox right above the "Make manifold" button.

title: Zero Area Faces detected as Non Manifold Edges
body:
blender 4.2 beta
addon version 1.0.0

As the original report got closed i checked and the described issue still seems relevant.

According to https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/4.1/addons/import_export/paper_model.html#usage the attached example should be detected as Zero Area Face.
> There are a few kinds of topology that are possible in Blender but not in paper reality:
    - N-gon faces (everything except triangles) that are not perfectly flat.
    - Zero-length edges (two vertices exactly in the same spot and connected by an edge)
    - Zero-area faces (typically their vertices lie all in line)

![grafik](/attachments/8f22cd20-bdc0-4576-880b-f4497db91965)

None Manifold edges on the other hand are usually when an edge is shared by more than two faces.

Original report: https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender-addons/issues/104715
